coverage.subsystem: Central and peripheral nervous system tumors
coverage.subtopic: Bilateral cerebellopontine-angle tumors and NF2/merlin loss
coverage.learning_objective: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are the hallmark of NF2-related schwannomatosis, which results from loss of the merlin tumor suppressor encoded by NF2 on chromosome 22.
Granulomatous macrophages can produce calcitriol through extrarenal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity, causing parathyroid-hormone-independent hypercalcemia in sarcoidosis.

coverage.subtopic: VHL loss, HIF stabilization, and angiogenic signaling
coverage.learning_objective: Loss of VHL in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma prevents HIF degradation, increasing VEGF and erythropoietin expression and producing a highly vascular tumor that may cause erythrocytosis.

coverage.subtopic: Noncontact pivot injury and restraint of anterior tibial translation
coverage.learning_objective: The anterior cruciate ligament restrains anterior tibial translation and rotational instability; a noncontact pivot with immediate hemarthrosis and a positive Lachman test strongly indicates ACL rupture.

coverage.subtopic: Functional asplenia, Howell-Jolly bodies, and encapsulated bacterial risk
coverage.learning_objective: Functional asplenia in sickle cell disease causes Howell-Jolly bodies because splenic macrophages can no longer remove erythrocyte nuclear remnants; loss of splenic filtration also increases risk from encapsulated bacteria.
Psoriasis is sustained by the IL-23/Th17 axis; IL-17-driven keratinocyte activation produces acanthosis, parakeratosis, and neutrophilic scale.

coverage.subtopic: Asthma, eosinophilia, IgE, mucus plugging, and central bronchiectasis
coverage.learning_objective: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a noninvasive Th2-predominant hypersensitivity reaction to airway colonization in asthma or cystic fibrosis, producing high IgE, eosinophilia, mucus plugging, and central bronchiectasis.

coverage.subtopic: Neutropenia, septate acute-angle hyphae, angioinvasion, and hemorrhagic infarction
coverage.learning_objective: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in neutropenic patients is characterized by septate acute-angle branching hyphae that invade blood vessels, causing thrombosis, hemorrhage, and infarction.
